the elucidation of the pathomechanism of the autosomal dominant form (AD-EDM) of Emery-Drefuss muscular dystrophy, a rare genetic disorder characterized by progressive weakness and wasting of skeletal muscle, joint contractures and cardiac conduction defects.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in this AD-EDM patient the R377H mutation in the LMNA gene leads to a reduction in lamin A levels and a concomitant alteration in the intranuclear distribution of LBR and the transcriptionally active form of RNA pol II.

the R377H mutation in LMNA leads to a reduction of lamin A, which in turn leads to the mislocalization of LBR and RNA pol II in the nuclei of muscle cells, which is likely the primary cause of EDMD pathology.
the nuclear envelope is not only the site of anchorage for the chromatin, but is also a functional compartment which plays an essential role in transcriptional regulation of the genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pathology of ED-EDMD is caused by an altered nuclear envelope structure and function.
the pathology in AD-EDMD patients is not only due to the loss of the nuclear envelope but also to the disruption of intranuclear organization.
the pathology of AD-EDMD is not due to the loss of the nuclear lamina but rather to a mislocalization of nuclear envelope proteins and/or to an altered chromatin organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a correct nuclear organization of the transcription machinery in muscle cells is crucial for the normal functioning of the cell.
the pathogenic mechanism of AD-EDMD is likely to be more complex than a simple loss of function of the A-type lamins.
a minor fraction of cells carrying the R377H mutation show a severe nuclear pathology.
